description: The contents of the Реєстр платіжної інфраструктури — above all the технологічні оператори платіжних послуг (ТОПП) section — were never opened, only located. This is the single most important list in the cell.
No verified programmatic access route was established for either bank.gov.ua or data.gov.ua; both blocked plain fetches, and the CKAN API path on data.gov.ua was identified but not exercised.

The register of registered payment SYSTEMS themselves — domestic and international (e.g. Visa, Mastercard, UAPAY, and other locally registered systems) — was identified only indirectly, via a vendor press release (uapay.ua) and NBU oversight reports, never as a retrieved list.

No banking-sector industry association or self-regulatory membership directory was searched in this run (e.g. НАБУ / Незалежна асоціація банків України, ЕМА / Українська міжбанківська асоціація членів платіжних систем, УМВБ, fintech associations).

Registers on the securities/capital-markets side (НКЦПФР — депозитарні установи, professional participants) and the insurance register were not covered, though some Printec-adjacent technology (identification, document workflow, self-service) is sold into those actors too.
No transliteration / alias table was built linking Ukrainian legal names (АТ КБ «ПриватБанк») to English forms, market brands and EDRPOU codes.
Only current-state registers were identified; no systematic archival route was established for reconstructing the actor population before the 2024 legal reset.

Buyer EDRPOU codes are confirmed for Oschadbank HQ (00032129), several Oschadbank regional branches (09322277, 09305480, 09338500, 09328601, 09353504), PrivatBank (14360570), Ukrgasbank (23697280) and the NBU (00032106), but the full branch list for Oschadbank and any code for Sense Bank are missing.
No verified CPV code list for ATM hardware, self-service kiosks, POS terminals, card personalisation equipment, core banking software or card-processing software.

It was not established which categories state-owned banks may procure outside Prozorro (banking-specific exemptions, security-sensitive IT, wartime derogations under the special procurement rules), nor how much of their ATM/processing spend that removes from view.

Technical specifications and contract PDFs attached to tender records were not sampled. These carry the brand and model detail (ATM model families, processing platform names, integration requirements) that the structured fields omit.

Russian-language variants of key terms (банкоматы, платёжные терминалы, процессинг) were not searched; legacy records and older supplier documentation from before the language transition may use them.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed reachable; all confidence scores reflect search-result evidence only.
PSP/acquirer and payment-institution employers (Fondy, Portmone, EasyPay, iPay, Platon, LeoGaming and NBU-registered payment institutions) have no mapped career sources.
Vendor-name keyword hunting was done via general web search, which indexes vacancy bodies poorly; on-site search of each board was not performed.
Vacancies expire and are deleted, so retrospective stack history cannot be reconstructed from live boards alone.
Engineering-community output beyond job boards — conference talks (DOU Day, Fwdays, iForum), YouTube tech talks and university/partner training programmes run by banks — was not scouted.
The two highest-density sources (LinkedIn, and CV databases) are the most access- and privacy-constrained.

Antimonopoly Committee (АМКУ) decision database and the DASU procurement-monitoring register were referenced as inputs to Clarity Project but were not located as standalone primary sources in this pass.
Beneficial-ownership and sanctions/PEP layers (e.g. Ukrainian sanctions registers, NAZK war-sponsors list) were only mentioned as aggregator features, not scouted as sources in their own right.
Russian-language variants of key terms (постачальник/поставщик, закупки, контрагент) were not used; some legacy Ukrainian corporate and court content is still Russian-language.
No check was made of whether international aggregators (OpenCorporates, OpenSanctions, Open Contracting Partnership mirrors) carry Ukrainian EDR/Prozorro data in a licence-friendlier form.

Bilateral donors and DFIs beyond the big four were not searched in this pass: KfW/DEG, SECO (explicitly named as an NBU partner), Sida, GIZ (implementer of EU4Business), Norfund/FMO/Proparco, and the Ukraine Development Fund vehicles. Several finance Ukrainian bank modernisation directly.

IFI accountability, evaluation and audit layers were not systematically mapped — EBRD Independent Evaluation Department, World Bank IEG, IFC CAO, and EU Court of Auditors reports. These retrospectively disclose what was actually delivered, by whom, and what failed.

Consultant-side self-disclosure was not mined: the firms winning IFI banking/payments assignments (management consultancies, Big Four, specialist payment advisers) publish project references, and their staff publish assignment detail on professional profiles. This often reveals scope and duration that the notice omits.

Ukrainian-language searching in this pass covered ЄБРР, МТД, Prozorro donor procurement and NBU/USAID project naming, but not Ukrainian terms for IFC (МФК), World Bank (Світовий банк) or EIB (ЄІБ) combined with payment-infrastructure vocabulary (платіжна система, СЕП, еквайринг, миттєві платежі).
ECEPP notice permalinks appear to be non-guessable (displayNoticeId / accessCode style), so no reliable listing-to-detail enumeration strategy was established in this pass.
Non-bank TPP/fintech side of open banking (aggregators, PFM apps, lenders using AIS data) is thinly covered — no directory of authorised or applying TPPs beyond the NBU register was harvested.

Private banks (Privat is state-owned but Raiffeisen, OTP, Credit Agricole, Universal/monobank, PUMB are not) procure outside Prozorro, so open-banking vendor selections at most of the market leave no procurement trace.

No developer-community sources collected (GitHub orgs for NBU/Diia API specs, DOU.ua job ads and forums, Ukrainian fintech Telegram channels) despite these being where implementation stacks are named earliest.
SEPA accession, cross-border instant payments and the digital hryvnia (е-гривня) pilot were not searched in this pass, though each drives its own vendor procurement adjacent to this cell.
English coverage over-represents foreign vendors (Tietoevry, Salt Edge) while Ukrainian coverage under-names vendors at all, preferring bank and regulator names.

No paid CEE/Ukraine banking-technology vendor-share research (IDC CEE, GlobalData, RBR/Datos Insights ATM & self-service studies) was located or priced in this pass. RBR/Datos 'Global ATM Market and Forecasts' style studies would be the canonical source for self-service installed base by country and vendor, but no Ukraine extract was confirmed.

This cell is English-first by design, so Ukrainian-language coverage here is deliberately limited to three local nodes (fintechinsider.com.ua, speka.ua, psm7.com) plus the UAFIC catalogue and NBU. Ukrainian-language transliteration variants for international vendor names (e.g. Дібольд Ніксдорф, Тієтоеврі, Прінтек) were not systematically harvested.

The strongest English analysis found for Emerging Europe dates to 2020, and several academic items are 2023 or earlier. Current-state international analytical coverage of Ukrainian banking technology (2024-2026) is sparse outside wire-style items.

Vendor-side global newsrooms (Mastercard, Visa, Tietoevry, BPC, OpenWay, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos) were identified as the origin of most English Ukraine deal detail but were not individually catalogued in this cell.
Several candidate URLs are section or homepage roots rather than confirmed deep links, and no URL in this slice has been checked for liveness.
Neither the PCI SSC assessor directory (country filter) nor the Держспецзв'язку attested-auditor register was actually opened in this pass; both are JS/portal resources.
Only a handful of Ukrainian processors/PSPs (UPC, ProCard, УкрКарт) were checked for certification disclosures; Tas Link, Fondy, Portmone, LiqPay/PrivatBank, Concord-successors and NovaPay were not.
PCI PIN Security, P2PE and PCI 3DS assessor coverage for Ukraine was not separately investigated, though these are the standards most tied to terminal and HSM vendor presence.
Russian-language material (still common in Ukrainian security/processing trade press and older certification announcements) was not searched, as the run scope specifies uk/en only.
CERT-UA and CSIRT-NBU advisory archives were identified but not enumerated; the historical depth of product/vendor mentions is unknown.

Sense Bank was not treated as an in-cell actor (state-owned since 2023 nationalisation) yet it surfaced as a leading example of AI adoption in Ukrainian banking; other privately-held mid-tier banks (Банк Південний / bank.com.ua, Ощад-adjacent private peers, Idea Bank, Кредобанк as Polish PKO-owned foreign bank) were also outside the named list.

Bank annual reports, ESG/sustainability reports and IFRS financial statements were not searched, although private banks disclose IT capex, digital-transformation programmes and sometimes supplier categories there.
Social channels other than one Telegram example were not enumerated — LinkedIn company pages and executive LinkedIn posts are where UA bank CIO/CTOs most often name vendors and go-live dates.

Bank careers/vacancy pages were not searched; job adverts for named platforms (core banking product names, card-processing systems, CRM) are one of the most reliable indirect disclosures of a private bank's vendor stack.
No vendor-side register exists yet for suppliers active in UA private banking beyond the incidental Corezoid/MiddleWare, Intellect Design Arena and Iliad Solutions hits.
This pass surfaced mostly 2024-2026 items; no systematic archive strategy was established for press items already removed from bank sites.
Russian-language variants of bank press material (still present in older PUMB/A-Bank slugs, e.g. 'pumb-zapustil-pervij-v-ukraine-banking-v-messendzh') were not searched.
ATM, cash-handling and cash-in-transit industry bodies remain uncovered — no Ukrainian sector association with a member directory was identified for this segment.
Two anchor rosters (UAFIC members, NABU member banks) have confirmed URLs but unretrieved contents due to JS rendering and rate limiting respectively.

IT Ukraine Association's 9 strategic partner IT clusters (regional bodies such as Lviv IT Cluster, Kharkiv IT Cluster) were identified as existing but not individually enumerated or scouted; each maintains its own member directory.
Only current-state member directories were captured; historical membership snapshots (which reveal entries, exits and consolidation) were not sourced beyond the 2023 vs 2025 fintech catalog pair.

The Ukrainian Credit-Banking Union's own official domain was not identified, and no scouting was done of insurance/credit-union associations named on EMA's partner page, which may carry payments-vendor members.
Hardware OEM references for Ukraine (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Hyosung, GRG) are entirely absent from vendor-published material.
Local and regional integrators/distributors — the parties that actually sign Ukrainian bank contracts — are only partially mapped (Transaction Systems found; others not).
Card production, personalisation and HSM/security vendors (IDEMIA, G+D, Thales, Utimaco) have no Ukraine-specific evidence trail.
Post-2022 vendor disclosure about Ukraine is sparse; pre-2022 disclosure may have been withdrawn.
Several candidate entry points were inferred (BPC corporate domain, vendor press indexes, Prozorro) rather than fetched in this pass.

Several candidate root URLs (incom.ua, systemgroup.com.ua root, deep2000.com.ua, cit-security.ua vs cit.net.ua, bmsserv.net entity attribution) were inferred from search-result metadata and not individually fetched in this pass.
Discovered firms are overwhelmingly Kyiv-centric. Regional service subcontractors (Lviv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Odesa) that actually perform field maintenance under national contracts were not enumerated.
No source was checked for post-2022 status: relocation, loss of eastern/southern branches, entity liquidation, or sanctions/ownership changes among integrators and CIT operators.

Two categories inferred but not yet populated: (a) NBU-side registers/requirements for CIT operators and cash-handling equipment approval, which would give an authoritative operator list; (b) Ukrainian trade media and job-board postings (robota.ua, work.ua) which name employers' vendor stacks and expansion in the ATM/POS service segment.
Published deployment case studies are rare in this cell; only SystemGroup was seen to maintain a /project/ case-study index, and none of it was bank-specific.
No scheme-side certification/approval registry specific to terminal hardware and EMV kernels used in Ukraine (EMVCo Letters of Approval, PCI PTS approved-device list) was captured in this pass.
Ukrainian-side scheme legal entities and their local representative offices (e.g. Visa's and Mastercard's registered UA entities) were not mapped to registry identifiers.
Russian-language legacy content (much pre-2022 scheme, processor and bank material in UA is in ru) was not searched, and no ru glossary terms were used.

Wartime disclosure practice may have reduced or delayed publication of scheme participant and infrastructure data since 2022; the archival dimension (Wayback snapshots of prostir.gov.ua participant lists and scheme press rooms) was not covered.
Scheme-run co-branding directories (which merchant/airline/retail co-brands exist on each scheme in UA) were not found as a structured source; only ad-hoc press releases.
E-wallet and P2P/remittance providers in Ukraine (as distinct from card-acquiring PSPs) were only lightly covered; no dedicated wallet-provider partner directory was located.
Merchant-win and bank-acquiring partnership announcements were found as isolated examples (WayForPay-LiqPay-Raiffeisen, iPay-Vchasno.Kasa) rather than as a systematically collectable stream.
The NBU Payment Infrastructure Register was identified conceptually but not located as a concrete, downloadable endpoint.
English-language sources for this cell are dominated by low-credibility aggregators (ensun, sourceforge, comparison blogs); the substantive material is almost entirely Ukrainian.
Self-service/ATM, core-banking replacement and card-processing vendor coverage is thin in Ukrainian trade media relative to neobank and payments-app coverage.
Paywalled/subscription tiers at Forbes Ukraine, NV Business, Mind and the Interfax wire will hide exactly the deal-detail paragraphs the cell exists to capture.
On-site search endpoints and archive pagination depth were not probed for any outlet, so historical backfill feasibility (how far back vendor-deal items are retrievable) is unknown.

Russian-language Ukrainian editions (several of these outlets historically published ru versions, and psm7 maintains multiple language paths) were not searched, since the run scope lists uk and en only.

The cell's actor map is currently seeded mainly by outlets and a few named entities (monobank/Fintech-IT Group, PayForce, UAPAY, Zen.com, e-Tender, SmartTender, SoftServe); no systematic vendor roster is yet in place to filter feeds.
Historical sponsor and exhibitor lists from pre-2022 UA events (and the 2022-2023 wartime gap when many events went online-only or were cancelled) were not sampled.

Event-related actor signal on social platforms (LinkedIn company/event pages, Facebook event pages such as the UAFintech page, Telegram announcement channels) was seen only incidentally and not systematically mapped.
Coverage is Kyiv-centric. Regional events (Lviv IT Arena, Львів International Economic Forum, Odesa/Dnipro business forums) were only glimpsed and their fintech/payments tracks were not examined.

Cybersecurity/anti-fraud event ecosystems adjacent to payments (EMA's SOC DAY Ukraine, BIS/InfoSecurity-type events) were identified only in passing; their sponsor lists carry the security-vendor layer of the payments stack.

This cell produced almost exclusively pointer sources; only one indirect source (bank self-published award pages) and no direct sources were recorded, which is expected for an events/awards cell but leaves speaker-bio-derived buyer-side decision-maker data uncollected.
